correctness.rationale: Equality of the full-circle squared Fourier magnitudes is equivalent to equality of every aperiodic autocorrelation, and coordinate magnitudes fix the support. After fixing the first coefficient to A>0, the outermost lag fixes the last coefficient C, giving immediate uniqueness for one or two nonzero points. For three points with unequal successive gaps, one lag isolates the middle coefficient. For equal gaps, middle candidates B,D obey A(D−B)+C·conj(D−B)=0 and |D|=|B|. Unequal endpoint magnitudes force equality; equal endpoint magnitudes reduce to a prescribed real part on a circle after a rotation. The other possible point gives precisely conjugate reflection times a unimodular scalar. For the four taps, expansion gives coefficientwise conjugates, all nonzero, and on the full circle the two quadratic factors have modulus |2cos(theta)±i s|. The shared support permits no nonidentity shift, the first tap fixes the scalar, and unequal endpoint magnitudes exclude conjugate reflection. These checks cover all s,t in the stated range. As a direct exact replay, the witness at (1,2) has nonnegative-lag autocorrelations (15,−8,5,−2) for each signal, obtained by summing the lagged products. The algebra in RESULT.md lines 24–79 is an all-parameter verification; the supplied finite-grid verifier was not executed as part of this audit.

evidence: For three support points, only equal successive gaps cause a repeated positive difference. For unequal gaps, the outermost lag and an isolated lag adjacent to the first support point force all phases once its phase is fixed. One- and two-point cases are even simpler.

For equal gaps both polynomial signals can be translated and compressed by the common step: the variable z^d still ranges over the full circle, reducing the case to degree two. In Theorem 2.2 the leading magnitude is proportional to (|beta_1||beta_2|)^(-1/2) at fixed autocorrelation. Switching one root beta to 1/conj(beta) preserves that coordinate magnitude only when |beta|=1, hence leaves the root unchanged. Switching both is conjugate reflection by Lemma 2.3. This includes coincident roots, viewed as multisets. Together with Theorem 3.6 at N=4, this yields the sharp cutoff.

evidence: For N=4, the earlier polynomials are X(z)=C(z−a)(z+1/a)(z−i b) and Y(z)=C(z−1/a)(z+a)(z−i b), with a,b>1. X(iz)/(C i b) and Y(iz)/(C i b) are exactly the frozen pair at s=a−1/a>0 and t=1/b in (0,1). The common substitution z→iz only rotates the angle and changes coordinate phases. The endpoints have unequal magnitudes, so the nontriviality notion in the frozen result holds as well.

Partner exchange changes the sign of s; z→−z changes the signs of both parameters; common scaled reversal P(z)→−z³P(1/z)/t sends t to 1/t for both polynomials. Together these reach all the frozen parameters.

evidence: The distinct catalogue record 5454fe769fbc states an exact existence criterion for positive magnitudes (A,B,C,D) on four consecutive positions: |AC−BD|<|A²−D²|<AC+BD. It also studies the number of nontrivial partner classes.
For the frozen family, take A=1, D=|t|, x=AC=√(1+s²t²), y=BD=|t|√(t²+s²). Then |x²−y²|=|1−t⁴|, so |x−y|=|1−t²|(1+t²)/(x+y)<|1−t²| since x+y>1+t². The right inequality follows from x+y>1+t²≥|1−t²|.

originality.rationale: Beinert and Plonka's 2016 Theorem 3.6 directly covers the four-tap existence and constructs exactly this entire two-parameter family up to data-preserving frequency shifts, exchange, and common reversal/scaling. It is not just an example with the same support cardinality. Their Theorem 2.2 and Lemma 2.3 also give the only potentially nontrivial lower-bound case by a short degree-two specialization; the other gaps have isolated autocorrelation terms. No claim that the earlier paper explicitly states the arbitrary-location cutoff theorem is needed for the failure: the lower bound and the exact construction follow mechanically from those comparisons.
residual_risks: The bounded comparison does not determine which source, if any, first stated the arbitrary-location cutoff explicitly. The targeted public search on that wording was unavailable; the failure relies on positive mathematical coverage, not that interruption.
The relative provenance of the two catalogue records and the indicated later survey example were not established.

value.rationale: The least-support question is natural and the treatment is a clear exposition, but the exact example and full proposed family are a reparameterized known construction. After that coverage is credited, the lower-bound remainder is a two-root specialization of the known general classification plus the elementary fact that unequal gaps isolate the relevant lag. No substantively new obstruction, ambiguity phenomenon, or classification survives in the original claim; making the known example an integer witness does not supply one.
